title: Where to Stay in Gangtok: MG Marg, Tadong and Beyond
meta_description: Which part of Gangtok to stay in: MG Marg and Tibet Road, Development Area, Paljor Stadium Road, Deorali, Tadong, upper Gangtok and Rumtek, with budgets.
summary: For a first visit, stay on or near MG Marg and Tibet Road, where you can walk to food, shops and tour desks; rooms cost ₹1,500–5,000. Development Area has hostels and quieter lanes, Deorali and Tadong are cheaper but need taxis, and Rumtek gives a calm night away from town. Book ahead for Puja, Diwali, New Year and May.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Gangtok is a long, steep ridge town, and where you sleep decides how much you walk, how much you spend on taxis and how much traffic you hear. Most of what visitors want is near the top: MG Marg, the car-free main street; Lal Bazaar below it; the tour desks that sell Tsomgo and Nathu La trips; and the cafés. Staying within ten minutes' walk of MG Marg saves money and time, even if the room costs a little more.

If you want quiet, choose a lane off the centre, in Development Area or upper Gangtok near Enchey, or spend a night at Rumtek. If you want the lowest price and do not mind taxis, look lower down in Deorali and Tadong. Prices here are indicative for 2025–26 and rise by a third or more in the Puja and Diwali weeks, from Christmas to New Year and in the May–June school holidays.

sections.heading: MG Marg and Tibet Road: the centre
paras: MG Marg was renovated in 2008 as a pedestrian mall, where vehicles, smoking, littering and spitting are banned. It is the town's evening meeting place, clean and well lit, lined with cafés, bookshops and outfitters. Tibet Road runs just above it, and the lanes between hold dozens of small hotels and guesthouses. From here you walk to Lal Bazaar, the tour desks, the ropeway and most restaurants, and the long-distance taxi stands are a short ride away.

Two long-standing family-run places we like are Hotel Sonam Delek on Tibet Road, with plain budget rooms and better valley-facing ones, and Mintokling Guest House, a garden compound in Sikkimese style a short walk from the mall and much quieter than it. Netuk House, a Sikkimese family home turned small guesthouse with painted woodwork and home-style meals, is the closest Gangtok comes to a heritage stay at a mid-range price.

The downside of the centre is noise from the roads just off the mall, and rooms on the lower floors of tall hotels that see little light. Ask for an upper floor, a room away from the road, and a valley view if you are paying for one.

If you travel with older parents or small children, check the approach before you book. Many central hotels sit up flights of steps from the nearest road, and some lanes off MG Marg are too narrow for cars, so a porter or a long carry may be needed for luggage. Ask the hotel how far the taxi drop is from the door, and whether there is a lift, before you pay a deposit.

sections.heading: Paljor Stadium Road and the NH10 side
paras: Below MG Marg, Paljor Stadium Road and the roads towards NH10 are busier with traffic but convenient for taxis, buses and early departures to Tsomgo or Siliguri. Hotel Tibet, an old hotel decorated in Tibetan style with painted pillars and thangkas, sits on Paljor Stadium Road a short walk from the mall. There are many plain budget hotels here at ₹1,500–3,500 a room.
This is a practical choice for a night before an early start or a late arrival. Walls can be thin and traffic starts early, so pack earplugs, and climb to MG Marg for your evenings.
If you come by reserved car, this side of town is also easier for parking, which is scarce near MG Marg. Ask the hotel whether parking is included or charged by the night.

sections.heading: Development Area and upper Gangtok
paras: Development Area, uphill from the centre, is mostly residential: government quarters, schools, family houses and, increasingly, backpacker hostels and small guesthouses. Dorm beds cost about ₹500–800 and private rooms ₹1,500–3,500. It is quieter than the centre and a 10–20 minute walk to MG Marg, though the walk back is steep. It suits backpackers and anyone staying a week.

Further up the ridge, towards Enchey Monastery, Ganesh Tok and the road to Tashi View Point, the town thins into greener lanes with some of the best views in Gangtok. It is good for couples who want quiet evenings and an early start for the viewpoints or Enchey's morning prayers. You will need taxis, at ₹100–300 a hop, to reach the centre.
Hostels here are a good place to find others to share a Tsomgo car or a Silk Route SUV, which cuts the biggest cost of a Gangtok trip.

sections.heading: Deorali, Tadong and Ranipool
paras: Deorali, below the centre, is where you find Do-drul Chorten, the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and the lower station of the ropeway. Hotels here are a little cheaper and the area is calmer in the evening. Tadong, further down along NH10, is a suburban area of offices, colleges and housing, with budget hotels and homestays at ₹1,200–3,000 a room. Ranipool, at the bottom of the valley, is where the road to Rumtek turns off.

These areas are good value if you are happy to use taxis, and handy if you arrive late from Siliguri. They are less good for a short first visit, because every evening on MG Marg means a taxi up and down, which adds ₹200–600 a day.

Pakyong, 31 km south-east of Gangtok, has a few hotels and homestays in a calmer district town. It is worth a night only if you have a flight from Pakyong Airport, whose services have been irregular, or as a stop on the way to Aritar and Rongli. Check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: A night at Rumtek or beyond
paras: For one calm night away from Gangtok's traffic, stay near Rumtek, 24 km away. You can walk to the monastery for morning prayers, wander down to the old Rumtek monastery and listen to nothing louder than prayer flags at night. Simple guesthouses near the monastery are cheap; Bamboo Retreat, an eco-minded place among terraced fields below the monastery road, is our comfort choice, at about ₹5,000–9,000 a room with meals.

Beyond Gangtok, the best way to see East Sikkim is to leave the capital and sleep in a village: Aritar for its lake, Padamchen and Zuluk on the Silk Route, Gnathang if you are acclimatised. Homestays there charge about ₹1,200–2,200 per person with dinner and breakfast.

Wherever you stay, book directly where you can, by phone or the property's own website, and ask for the room you actually want: valley view, upper floor, heater, twin or double. Read recent reviews for noise and hot water rather than for star ratings. Pay deposits only to the hotel, not to touts at the taxi stand, and in the off-season walk in and compare two or three places before you choose.

Ask whether the hotel has a heater from November to February.

Confirm parking if you arrive in a reserved car; the centre has little.

faqs.q: Which is the best area to stay in Gangtok?
faqs.a: For a first visit, stay on or near MG Marg and Tibet Road. You can walk to cafés, Lal Bazaar, the ropeway and the tour desks that arrange Tsomgo and Nathu La trips, and save on taxis. Double rooms cost about ₹2,000–5,500 off-peak. For quiet, choose upper Gangtok or a night at Rumtek.

faqs.q: Where do backpackers stay in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Mostly in Development Area and the lanes around Tibet Road, where hostels offer dorm beds for about ₹500–800 and private rooms from about ₹1,500. Development Area is quieter and a 10–20 minute walk from MG Marg, with a steep climb back. Book ahead in October and May.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay on MG Marg or away from it?
faqs.a: Near it, but not on the noisiest stretch. MG Marg is car-free, but the roads just off it carry traffic, and lower rooms in tall hotels can be dark. Choose a hotel in a lane within ten minutes' walk, on an upper floor, away from the road, for the best of both.

faqs.q: Is Tadong a good place to stay in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Tadong is good value, with budget hotels at about ₹1,200–3,000 a room, and handy for late arrivals from Siliguri. But it is several kilometres below the centre, so evenings on MG Marg mean taxis, adding ₹200–600 a day. It suits longer stays and travellers who do not mind taxis.

faqs.q: How much does a hotel in Gangtok cost?
faqs.a: Dorm beds cost about ₹500–800, budget doubles ₹1,500–3,000 and mid-range rooms ₹3,000–5,500 off-peak. Heritage-style guesthouses such as Netuk House cost about ₹4,500–7,500 with breakfast. Prices rise by a third or more in Puja, Diwali, New Year and May weeks. All prices are indicative for 2025–26.

faqs.q: Should I stay a night at Rumtek?
faqs.a: Yes, if you want quiet. A night near Rumtek lets you attend morning prayers at the monastery and walk to the old monastery without day-trip crowds. Simple guesthouses are cheap, and Bamboo Retreat, below the monastery road, costs about ₹5,000–9,000 a room with meals. It is about an hour from Gangtok.

faqs.q: When should I book hotels in Gangtok?
faqs.a: A month or more ahead for Durga Puja, Diwali, Christmas to New Year and the May–June school holidays, when central rooms fill and prices rise. At other times, a few days ahead is usually enough, and walk-in rates can be lower in the monsoon and in January and February.

Many do not have central heating. Most mid-range hotels provide electric heaters, sometimes for an extra charge, and better rooms have heavy blankets. From November to February, ask about heaters when you book. Nights fall to about 4–6 °C in town in mid-winter.

faqs.q: Can I find a homestay in Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes, a few family homestays operate in Gangtok's residential areas and in Tadong, but the real homestay experience in East Sikkim is in villages such as Aritar, Padamchen and Zuluk, at about ₹1,200–2,200 per person with dinner and breakfast. Use Gangtok as a base for permits and day trips.
